questions.question: An agent rewrites a whole 800-line file to change one line, and a function disappears. What's the root cause?
options: The tool lets it overwrite whole files instead of making small exact edits to text it has read
Python files can't be edited by agents
questions.explanation: Tool design decides how careful an agent can be. Exact, small edits keep unseen code safe.

questions.question: The model calls edit_file on a file it hasn't read in this session. What does the lesson's tool do?
questions.explanation: Edits must be based on content the model has actually seen, and that hasn't changed since.

questions.question: old='calc_total' appears twice in the file. What should the tool return?
options: An error listing the line numbers, suggesting more context or replace_all=true
questions.explanation: The error tells the model exactly how to succeed on the next call.

questions.question: A search returns 300 hits. What should the model see?
options: The first N hits plus '… M more matches. Narrow the pattern or the glob.'
questions.explanation: Capping protects the context; reporting the hidden count tells the model to refine the search.

questions.question: In the lesson's test, old='  return sum' unexpectedly succeeded and broke indentation. Why?
options: Two spaces + 'return sum' is a substring of the real line's four-space version; a too-short old string matched mid-line
questions.explanation: Exact match is necessary but not sufficient. Use whole lines in old, and read the returned diff.

questions.question: Which is the best error when old isn't found but matches with different indentation?
options: 'Line 1 matches if you ignore indentation: <the real line>. Copy whitespace exactly.'
questions.explanation: Show the real text and the fix. Silent fuzzy edits risk changing the wrong place.
